problems.subject: SAE Review & Response - DNLI-001 Site 203 Pt 203-005 - Hospitalization (Fall)
problems.summary: Urgent SAE requiring sponsor review and response. Participant 203-005 (Part B) hospitalized following fall at home with reported dizziness. Site PI assessed as 'possibly related' to investigational product. Actions needed: Review SAE form and hospital documentation, coordinate with Medical Monitor (Sarah Chen) for causality assessment, determine expectedness, confirm regulatory reporting timelines, and provide feedback to site CRA (Maria Garcia) on any additional documentation requirements.

todos.description: Review SAE form (DNLI-001_SAE_Form_203-005_Fall.pdf) and hospital admission summary for completeness, accuracy, and consistency with 24-hour reporting requirements
Review protocol and Investigator's Brochure to determine if hospitalization due to fall with dizziness is an 'expected' event for Part B participants, document finding
Coordinate with Medical Monitor (Sarah Chen) to request causality assessment and timeline for response - forward SAE documentation and site PI's 'possibly related' assessment
Confirm regulatory reporting timelines based on expectedness determination and prepare notification to site CRA (Maria Garcia) with feedback on documentation and any additional requirements

threads.name: Low IP Stock Alert - Patient Visit Before Scheduled Resupply
threads.description: A notification from a site coordinator regarding investigational product inventory timing. The site has a patient scheduled for dosing in 5 days, but this visit falls 5 days before the normal monthly resupply shipment is due to arrive. The coordinator is proactively requesting guidance on expediting the shipment or managing inventory.

messages.content:
Hi Alex,

Hope you're doing well.

I wanted to reach out regarding our investigational product inventory timing at Site 405 (Riverside Clinical Research) for study DNLI-001.

We have patient 405-2008 scheduled for their Week 12 dosing visit this Friday, November 1st at 9:00 AM. During our routine inventory review today, our pharmacy noted that we currently have 2 kits remaining in stock. The protocol requires 3 kits to be available on-site for proper randomization backup according to the pharmacy manual.

Our normal monthly resupply shipment is scheduled to arrive on Wednesday, November 6th - which means this patient visit is happening 5 days before our usual restock day. Our last shipment arrived about 3 weeks ago, so we're just in that gap between shipments.

Could you please advise on the best approach:
1. Is it possible to expedite the November shipment to arrive by Thursday, October 31st (day before the visit)?
2. Alternatively, should we consider rescheduling the patient visit to the following week after the resupply arrives?
3. Are there any other sites in the region that might have excess inventory we could coordinate a transfer from?

We have some flexibility with this patient's schedule if needed, and Dr. Patterson is aware of the situation. Just wanted to get ahead of this to avoid any issues.

Please let me know what you think is the best path forward.

Thank you!

Best regards,

Jennifer Martinez, CCRC
Senior Clinical Research Coordinator
Riverside Clinical Research Center - Site 405
(555) 234-7890
jennifer.martinez@riversidecrc.org

Sarah Chen, CCRP

messages.content:
Dear Alex,

This email is to urgently inform you of a significant protocol deviation that occurred today at our site (102) for study DNLI-001.

This morning, participant 102-2005, enrolled in Part B (FTD cohort), was inadvertently administered a double dose of the investigational product during their scheduled Visit 5 infusion.

We have documented the event and completed the attached Protocol Deviation form. We require immediate guidance on the necessary follow-up, safety monitoring, and reporting procedures. Please escalate this to the study's Medical Monitor as soon as possible for their assessment and recommendations.

Best regards,

Dr. Sarah Chen

Maplewood Clinical Research Center
(555) 123-4567
